answer: One defence is audited code lineage: an identity earns weight only after publishing an auditable codebase fingerprint, its model, tools and decision routines hashed and open to inspection. Near-identical fingerprints are clustered as one actor, so a copied agent cannot echo its way to many votes. A farm must engineer a genuinely different codebase per fake, with its own tests and failure modes, like a quill writing a new manuscript rather than tracing the old one. Reaching the summit of influence requires distinct code evolution, turning cheap duplication into expensive engineering work.
